criteria.name: Cites Administrative Procedure Act
criteria.description: Comment explicitly references the APA or specific APA provisions (e.g., notice requirements, arbitrary-and-capricious standard).
criteria.rationale: APA citations demonstrate knowledge of the legal framework governing rulemaking and may strengthen procedural challenges.

criteria.name: Cites enabling statute or organic act
criteria.description: Comment references the specific statutory authority under which the agency is acting (e.g., Clean Air Act, Securities Exchange Act).
criteria.rationale: Statutory grounding shows the commenter understands the bounds of agency authority and can identify ultra vires concerns.

criteria.name: References specific regulatory sections
criteria.description: Comment identifies particular CFR citations, proposed rule section numbers, or existing regulation text.
criteria.rationale: Precise regulatory references enable targeted agency response and show careful reading of the rule text.

criteria.name: Invokes procedural defects
criteria.description: Comment argues that the rulemaking process itself violates procedural requirements (e.g., inadequate notice period, insufficient analysis).
criteria.rationale: Procedural challenges can invalidate a rule and force agencies to restart the process.

criteria.name: Raises constitutional issues
criteria.description: Comment identifies potential constitutional violations (e.g., First Amendment, Takings Clause, non-delegation).
criteria.rationale: Constitutional arguments escalate legal stakes and may trigger heightened agency scrutiny.

criteria.name: Cites case law or precedent
criteria.description: Comment references judicial decisions, agency precedents, or analogous rulemakings.
criteria.rationale: Legal precedent grounds arguments in binding or persuasive authority.

criteria.name: Asserts conflict with existing rules
criteria.description: Comment identifies inconsistencies between the proposed rule and current regulations or statutory mandates.
criteria.rationale: Internal contradictions create legal vulnerability and may require reconciliation.

criteria.name: Provides quantitative data or statistics
criteria.description: Comment includes numerical evidence, cost figures, prevalence rates, or other quantitative support.
criteria.rationale: Hard data strengthens factual claims and helps agencies satisfy reasoned-decision-making requirements.

criteria.name: Cites peer-reviewed research
criteria.description: Comment references published studies, scientific literature, or expert reports.
criteria.rationale: Academic research lends credibility and may fill gaps in the agency's technical record.

criteria.name: Demonstrates technical or domain expertise
criteria.description: Comment displays specialized knowledge (e.g., engineering details, industry-specific terminology, scientific principles).
criteria.rationale: Expertise signals that the comment draws on professional knowledge rather than lay opinion.

criteria.name: Presents original analysis or modeling
criteria.description: Comment includes new calculations, simulations, or analytical frameworks not in the agency's proposal.
criteria.rationale: Original analysis provides information the agency may not have considered.

criteria.name: Identifies data gaps or methodological flaws
criteria.description: Comment critiques the agency's evidentiary basis, pointing to missing data, faulty assumptions, or analytical errors.
criteria.rationale: Methodological challenges can undermine the agency's technical justification.

criteria.name: Offers empirical evidence of impact
criteria.description: Comment provides real-world examples, case studies, or field data showing how the rule would affect specific entities.
criteria.rationale: Concrete evidence of impact helps agencies assess practical consequences.

criteria.name: Presents cost-benefit analysis
criteria.description: Comment quantifies expected costs, benefits, or economic effects of the proposed rule or alternatives.
criteria.rationale: Cost-benefit analysis is often legally required and may reveal whether benefits justify costs.

criteria.name: Targets specific regulatory text
criteria.description: Comment identifies exact sentences, definitions, or provisions it seeks to change.
criteria.rationale: Precise targeting makes it clear what the commenter wants modified.

criteria.name: Proposes alternative regulatory language
criteria.description: Comment drafts replacement text, definitions, or standards the agency could adopt.
criteria.rationale: Draft language gives the agency a concrete alternative and may be incorporated directly.

criteria.name: Recommends a clear modification
criteria.description: Comment articulates a specific action (e.g., extend deadline, narrow scope, add exemption) rather than general opposition.
criteria.rationale: Actionable requests are easier for agencies to address than vague objections.

criteria.name: Identifies affected entities or activities
criteria.description: Comment specifies which industries, products, geographic areas, or practices the rule would impact.
criteria.rationale: Scope clarity helps agencies understand distributional effects and tailor responses.

criteria.name: Distinguishes multiple sub-issues
criteria.description: Comment breaks down concerns into discrete points (e.g., numbered objections, separate regulatory sections).
criteria.rationale: Structured comments are easier to parse and respond to point-by-point.

criteria.name: Suggests implementation details
criteria.description: Comment addresses how the rule would be administered (e.g., reporting mechanisms, compliance timelines, enforcement).
criteria.rationale: Implementation feasibility is critical to effective regulation.

criteria.name: Requests specific exemptions or carve-outs
criteria.description: Comment asks for defined categories to be excluded from the rule's requirements.
criteria.rationale: Narrow exemption requests may be easier for agencies to accommodate than broad objections.

criteria.name: Identifies unintended consequences
criteria.description: Comment explains how the rule could produce effects the agency did not anticipate (e.g., market distortions, perverse incentives).
criteria.rationale: Unintended-consequence arguments help agencies foresee and mitigate harms.

criteria.name: Distinguishes facts from opinions
criteria.description: Comment clearly separates factual assertions from value judgments or policy preferences.
criteria.rationale: Factual claims are easier for agencies to verify or rebut.

criteria.name: Provides logical structure or sequencing
criteria.description: Comment follows a clear argumentative flow (e.g., claim-evidence-conclusion, if-then reasoning).
criteria.rationale: Logical coherence makes arguments more persuasive and easier to evaluate.

criteria.name: Addresses agency's stated justification
criteria.description: Comment engages directly with the agency's rationale for the rule (as stated in the preamble or RIA).
criteria.rationale: Responsive arguments show the commenter read the proposal and understands the agency's position.

criteria.name: Acknowledges trade-offs or counterarguments
criteria.description: Comment recognizes competing interests, limitations of its own position, or reasons favoring the rule.
criteria.rationale: Balanced arguments signal good faith and may be more credible.

criteria.name: Proposes alternatives that achieve agency goals
criteria.description: Comment suggests different means to accomplish the agency's stated objectives.
criteria.rationale: Constructive alternatives support the agency's mission while addressing commenter concerns.

criteria.name: Uses analogies or comparisons
criteria.description: Comment draws parallels to other rules, jurisdictions, or situations to illustrate a point.
criteria.rationale: Analogies can clarify complex issues and suggest tested approaches.

criteria.name: Identifies commenter affiliation or role
criteria.description: Comment states whether the commenter is an industry group, NGO, state agency, academic, or individual.
criteria.rationale: Affiliation signals the commenter's perspective and potential stake in the outcome.

criteria.name: Demonstrates directly affected status
criteria.description: Comment explains how the rule would concretely impact the commenter's operations, rights, or interests.
criteria.rationale: Directly affected parties often have superior information about practical effects.

criteria.name: Represents collective or coordinated view
criteria.description: Comment indicates it speaks for multiple entities (e.g., 'many commenters,' trade association, coalition).
criteria.rationale: Collective comments may signal broader consensus or concern.

criteria.name: Claims expertise or professional credentials
criteria.description: Comment establishes the commenter's qualifications (e.g., 'as a licensed engineer,' 'based on 20 years in the field').
criteria.rationale: Credentials lend authority and suggest the comment draws on specialized knowledge.

criteria.name: Provides sector or industry context
criteria.description: Comment situates the rule within broader market conditions, industry practices, or competitive dynamics.
criteria.rationale: Contextual information helps agencies understand real-world implications.

criteria.name: Uses precise technical terminology
criteria.description: Comment employs domain-appropriate language (e.g., regulatory terms of art, industry jargon) accurately.
criteria.rationale: Precision reduces ambiguity and signals familiarity with the subject matter.

criteria.name: Maintains narrow topical focus
criteria.description: Comment addresses a well-defined issue rather than raising diffuse or tangential concerns.
criteria.rationale: Focused comments are easier to categorize and respond to substantively.

criteria.name: Avoids inflammatory or adversarial tone
criteria.description: Comment frames objections constructively rather than attacking the agency or using polemical language.
criteria.rationale: Professional tone may encourage more sympathetic consideration.

criteria.name: Expresses clear support or opposition
criteria.description: Comment unambiguously states whether it favors or opposes the rule (or specific provisions).
criteria.rationale: Clear positions help agencies tally and categorize feedback.

criteria.name: Provides context for lay understanding
criteria.description: Comment explains technical or legal concepts in accessible terms (e.g., defining acronyms, summarizing background).
criteria.rationale: Clarity aids agency staff and public reviewers who may lack specialized knowledge.

criteria.name: Frames issue as urgent or time-sensitive
criteria.description: Comment emphasizes immediacy, deadlines, or irreversible harms if the rule proceeds.
criteria.rationale: Urgency framing may prompt faster or more careful agency attention.

criteria.name: Requests additional process or analysis
criteria.description: Comment asks for extended comment periods, public hearings, supplemental environmental review, or other procedural steps.
criteria.rationale: Process requests may delay finalization and create opportunities for further input.
